speaker: Vincent Gramoli
point: Accountable consensus: anyone who tries to double spend can be identified, because the protocol produces an undeniable proof of fraud.
caption: Founder Vincent Gramoli explains why cheaters get caught on Redbelly: accountable consensus produces an undeniable proof of fraud.

speaker: Vincent Gramoli
point: Every Redbelly node accepts from day one that governance can upgrade the protocol, so a new version rolls out automatically instead of splitting the chain in two.
caption: Vincent Gramoli explains how Redbelly nodes upgrade themselves when governance decides, with no hard fork and no split chain.

speaker: Matt Mills
point: In Project Acacia, investors used the AUDM stablecoin to buy into and cash out of a fund through Tokeniser, with each swap settling straight away instead of over days.
caption: In Project Acacia, buying into a fund or cashing out became an instant swap of AUDM stablecoin for fund units, with no waiting on paperwork.

speaker: Vincent Gramoli
point: Tokenising invoices in Project Acacia showed that the value is in the workflow around the token, where the invoice works as a promise of payment, not in the digital copy itself.
caption: A tokenised invoice is only a digital PDF until a workflow uses it, says Vincent Gramoli on what Project Acacia showed.

speaker: Matt Mills
point: Tokeniser answers the 'how' of real-world asset tokenisation with a familiar web platform that brings issuers, their investors and their tokens onto the Redbelly Network.
caption: Matt Mills on why Tokeniser exists: a familiar platform that brings issuers and their investors onto the Redbelly Network.

speaker: Alan Burt
point: Every regulated asset needs a registry of who owns what, so Redbelly acquired Liquidise's registry business and rebranded it Tokeniser to cover an asset's whole life cycle.
caption: Every regulated asset starts with a registry, which is why Redbelly acquired Liquidise's registry business and relaunched it as Tokeniser.
